post.title: I doubled gravity and all 100 AI probes missed the Moon. 8 generations later: 93
post.caption: Doubling gravity took my AI probes from 92 Moon hits to 0. Gen 1: 5 of 100 reached the Moon. Gen 3: 37. Gen 8: 79. Gen 11: 92. Then at gen 12 I doubled the pull of the planet in their path and not one probe made it. Gen 14: 39. Gen 17: 70. Gen 20: 93, one better than before the change. Each probe is a small neural network; the best flyers each generation get copied with small mutations, and nobody tells them how to fly.
post.pinned: Each probe is a tiny neural net steering its thrust. Every generation the best flyers get copied with random mutations. At gen 12 the planet's gravity doubles (9000 to 18000) and they have to relearn the route.
post.notes: Seed 1785. Per-gen hits: 1:5 3:37 8:79 11:92 12:0 14:39 17:70 20:93. mu 9000 -> 18000 = 2x. 92 - 0 = 92 lost. 93 - 92 = 1 better. 20 - 12 = 8 gens. Idea test: question yes, reaction yes, unrealistic yes (0 then 93), relatable no = 3 of 4.
